answer: Latency-Shaped Admission Pacing. Each new identity must sustain a minimal inter-arrival delay between its first transactions, measured as a variance floor in its early traffic—a timing signal the network verifies before granting full throughput. Like a juniper vine that only climbs once rooted, the agent must accumulate slow, steady activity before scaling. Attackers pay wall-clock time per identity: N fakes require N×delay in parallel capacity, making bulk sybils linear in real time rather than cheap.
